title: Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation · 71152A
text:
Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation                                            71152A
This violation of very low safety significance was identified by the licensee and has been
entered into the licensee corrective action program and is being treated as a non-cited
violation, consistent with Section 2.3.2 of the Enforcement Policy.




Violation:

Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 55.25 requires that if, during the term of
the license, the licensed reactor operator or senior reactor operator develops a permanent
physical or mental condition that causes the licensee to fail to meet the requirements of
10 CFR 55.21, the facility shall notify the Commission within 30 days of learning of the
diagnoses, in accordance with 10 CFR 50.74(c). For conditions for which a conditional license
(as described in 10 CFR 55.33(b)) where a license condition is requested, the facility licensee
shall provide medical certification on Form NRC 396, “Certification of Medical Examination by
Facility Licensee” (as described in 10 CFR 55.23).

Contrary to the above, the facility licensee failed to notify the Commission within 30 days of the
diagnoses of changes in medical conditions on three separate occasions for licensed
operators that developed permanent physical conditions which caused the licensed operators
to fail to meet the requirements of 10 CFR 55.21. Specifically, on March 31, 2025, a license
class applicant informed the facility’s medical examiner that he was taking prescribed
medication. When the medical examiner completed the physical examination report to the
facility, the condition for the prescribed medication was not reported and the medical examiner
recommended that no conditions be placed on the license when issued. Once licensed, the
senior operator continued to take the medication as prescribed when performing licensed
duties. The licensed operator was later evaluated by the medical examiner as no longer
requiring the medication and the prescription was discontinued. As the operator no longer was
prescribed medication, the facility licensee determined that the operator license was correct
(no restrictions) and no report was now required.

Subsequently, on January 20, 2026, and on February 12, 2026, during biennial license
physical examinations the designated medical examiner determined that two licensed
operators did not meet the near vision requirement in ANSI/ANS-3.4-1983, “Medical
Certification and Monitoring of Personnel Requiring Operator Licenses for Nuclear Power
Plants.” The two licensed operators were administratively restricted from performing licensed
duties until they received and wore their prescription lenses.

On April 1, 2026, the facility licensee identified that the NRC had not been notified, via
Form 396, “Certification of Medical Examination by Facility Licensee,” about the permanent
change in the two licensed operators’ vision and their need for prescription lenses to maintain
their medical qualifications for their operator licenses. As noted, the facility did not determine
that the missed “take medication as prescribed” license condition for the licensed operator in
the first example must also be reported. The NRC was notified of the other two operators’
conditions in a letter dated April 2, 2026, with the revised NRC Form 396s sent to the NRC on
April 13, 2026.

The inspectors verified that the licensed operators did not perform licensed duties from the
time their changes in medical condition were identified until they received and wore their
prescription lenses. The inspectors also verified that the three licensed operators did not
commit any errors or been involved in any operational mishaps while performing licensed
duties from the time they received and wore their prescription lenses until the NRC was
notified and received the individuals updated NRC Form 396s with their lenses restriction.

Significance/Severity: Severity Level IV. The inspectors determined the violation to be a
Severity Level IV violation similar to Example 6.9.d.9 in the NRC Enforcement Policy.



Specifically, the licensee failed to make a report required by 10 CFR 50.74(c) to inform the
NRC of changes in operators’ medical conditions. In addition, the individuals adhered to the
ANSI 3.4 requirements to mitigate the changes in their medical conditions while performing
licensed duties.

Corrective Action References: CR 26013325 and CR 26014029

title: Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation · 71111.20
text:
Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation                                         71111.20
 This violation of very low safety significance was identified by the licensee and has been
 entered into the licensee corrective action program and is being treated as a non-cited
 violation, consistent with Section 2.3.2 of the Enforcement Policy.
 Violation:

 Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 26, “Fitness for Duty Programs,”
 Subpart 205, “Work Hours,” requires, in part, that licensees shall control work hours so an
 individual’s hours worked do not exceed 16 hours in any 24-hour period, 26 hours in any
 48-hour period, and 72 hours in any 7-day period. Additionally, it requires, in part, that
 licensees shall ensure that individuals have, at a minimum, a 34-hour break in any 9-day
 period.

 Contrary to the above, between March 28, 2026, and April 3, 2026, the licensee failed to
 ensure that individuals subject to the requirements of 10 CFR Part 26 complied with the
 work hour limitations and scheduling restrictions of Part 26. Specifically, the licensee failed
 to adequately schedule and control the work hours of 3 individuals performing work
 covered by the restrictions of 10 CFR Part 26 by not ensuring that the individuals ’ work
 hours did not exceed 72 hours in any 7-day period. Additionally, the licensee failed to
 ensure that the same individuals received at least a 34-hour break in any 9-day period.

 Significance/Severity: Green. The inspectors assessed the significance of the finding
 using IMC 0609 Appendix A, “The Significance Determination Process (SDP) for Findings
 At-Power.” Using Exhibit 2, “Mitigating Systems Screening Questions,” of IMC 0609
 Appendix A, Section A, the inspectors answered “No” to all of the questions, screening the
 finding to Green, as the work completed by the three individuals was verified by individuals
 who did meet the requirements of the Part 26 work hours restrictions, ensuring that the
 equipment maintained either its operability or functionality.

title: Minor Violation · 71152A
text:
Minor Violation                                                                      71152A
Minor Violation: On February 16, 2026, the inspectors reviewed the licensee’s causal analysis
(CR 25015026) and associated corrective actions related to the inadvertent installation of
non-quality parts in the safety-related emergency diesel generators (EDGs) and main steam
safety system. Specifically, on or about December 13, 2025, the licensee identified that
multiple purchase orders that were issued for safety-related Swagelok check valves in
the fuel and/or air start systems for EDG 1-1 and EDG 1-2, along with refurbishment of
safety-related main steam safety valves in the main steam safety system, did not conform to
the procurement documents to ensure quality. Several of the purchased items were received
and installed in the plant, which included the EDG 1-1 fuel oil priming pump P-210A
discharge check valve (CK-DE400), EDG 1-2 fuel oil priming pump P-210B discharge check
valve (CK-DE401), and main steam safety valve (RV-0701).

The EDGs supply backup electrical power to various safety-related buses that power
plant equipment to ensure safe shut down and maintain core cooling if offsite power was lost.
The main steam safety system (steam generated from steam generators) contains 12
spring-loaded safety valves that function as overpressure protection in accordance with
American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel (B&PV)
code, Section III, Rules for Construction of Nuclear Facility Components. Title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion VII, “Control of
Purchased Material, Equipment, Services” requires, in part, that measures shall be
established to assure that purchased material, equipment, and services, whether purchased
directly or through contractors and subcontractors, conform to procurement documents.
These quality assurance processes are essential to provide reasonable assurance that
structures, systems, and/or components installed in the plant would perform their specified
safety function(s).

The licensee’s causal analysis concluded that procurement and receipt inspection processes
that support implementation of the Palisades quality assurance program were not consistently
performed with sufficient rigor to ensure safety-related components satisfy the quality
objectives identified on the qualified suppliers list (QSL), safety-related purchase orders,
and supporting quality documentation requirements prior to receipt acceptance or installation.
Supply chain did not perform the required verification and validation of controls and
procedures to ensure only qualified safety-related components were procured and installed.
For EDG 1-1 and EDG 1-2, Swagelok valves were purchased directly from Swagelok.
However, Swagelok was not specifically listed on the Palisades QSL to provide safety-related
valves and, therefore, was considered an unqualified supplier. For the main steam safety
valve refurbishments, although the supplier had maintained a quality assurance program, the
specific facility where repair work had been performed was a satellite location that had not
been audited and, therefore, should not have been on the Palisades QSL. A qualified supplier
was a supplier who had undergone a quality and technical evaluation by responsible
organizations and was approved to provide specific material or services as identified on the
QSL. In addition, the main steam safety valve purchase order stated, in part, repairs and
steam certification testing shall be performed in accordance with Holtec approved repair and
testing procedures as approved by the Palisades Program Engineer. On October 28, 2025,
the licensee identified that the repair plan had not been reviewed and approved by the
responsible engineer.

The inspectors determined that the licensee’s failure to assure that purchased material,
equipment, and services conformed to procurement documents in accordance with


10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion VII, “Control of Purchased Material, Equipment,
Services,” was a performance deficiency. Specifically, documentation associated with several
emergency diesel generator and main steam safety system components, procured as
safety-related, did not satisfy purchase order requirements upon receipt and were not
identified during material receipt inspection. Licensee quality Procedure MP-120, “Material
Receipt,” Revision 0, step 7.7.6 states, in part, for quality inspection “supplier documentation
such as certificate of conformance, supporting documents or certificate of analysis attesting
to acceptable test results shall be reviewed in a manner to ensure purchase order
requirements are satisfied. Documentation received from a third-party dedicator and/or the
CGD [commercial grade dedication] lab shall also be reviewed in a reasonable manner to
verify accuracy, traceability to the purchase order, receipt lot/batch, etc. ensuring the CGD
acceptance criteria is satisfied.”

Screening: The inspectors determined the performance deficiency was minor. The main
steam system and EDG 1-1 had not been returned to service since Palisades re-entered
the Reactor Oversight Process on August 25, 2025, nor were required to be operable
per technical specifications in the mode of applicability (plant was in defueled condition).
EDG 1-2 was returned to service (operable) on November 11, 2025, to support irradiated
fuel movements in the spent fuel pool in accordance with Technical Specification 3.8.2,
Alternating Current Sources - Shutdown. Irradiated fuel movements commenced on
November 17, 2025, and completed on December 9, 2025. The licensee performed a
past operability evaluation regarding the installation of the non-quality (commercial grade,
not safety-related) fuel oil priming pump P210-B check valve (CK-DE401) and reasonably
concluded there were no operational impacts to EDG 1-2 during the periodic movement of
irradiated fuel in the spent fuel pool and the EDG remained capable of performing its intended
safety function. In addition, a supplier evaluation was performed on the main steam safety
valve repair facility satellite location and demonstrated compliance with applicable technical
and quality assurance requirements. Therefore, the inspectors determined the performance
deficiency was not reasonably viewed as a precursor to a significant event; if left uncorrected,
would not have the potential to lead to a more significant concern; was either not associated
with or did not adversely impact any of the cornerstone objectives; and was similar to
Inspection Manual Chapter 0612, Appendix E, “Examples of Minor Issues,” example 5.c.

Enforcement: 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B, Criterion VII, “Control of Purchased Material,
Equipment, Services” states, in part, measures shall be established to assure that purchased
material, equipment, and services, whether purchased directly or through contractors and
subcontractors, conform to the procurement documents. These measures shall include
provisions, as appropriate, for source evaluation and selection, objective evidence of quality
furnished by the contractor or subcontractor, inspection at the contractor or subcontractor
source, and examination of products upon delivery. Documentary evidence that material and
equipment conform to the procurement requirements shall be available at the nuclear power
plant site prior to installation or use of such material and equipment. This documentary
evidence shall be retained at the nuclear power plant and shall be sufficient to identify the
specific requirements, such as codes, standards, or specifications, met by the purchased
material or equipment. The effectiveness of the control of quality by contractors and
subcontractors shall be assessed by the applicant or designee at intervals consistent with
the importance, complexity, and quantity of the product or services.

Contrary to the above, from July 25, 2025, [date of first Swagelok valve receipt inspection -
September 9, 2025, for main steam safety valve RV-0701] to December 13, 2025, [date CR
for Swagelok check valves written - November 4, 2025, for RV-0701] the licensee failed to


  assure that purchased material, equipment, and services conformed to procurement
  documents. Specifically, documentation associated with several emergency diesel generator
  and main steam safety system components procured as safety-related did not satisfy
  purchase order requirements upon receipt and were not identified during material receipt
  inspection.

  This failure to comply with 10 CFR 50, Appendix B, Criterion VII, “Control of Purchased
  Material, Equipment, Services” constitutes a minor violation that is not subject to enforcement
  action in accordance with the NRC’s Enforcement Policy.

title: Minor Violation · 71111.21N.05
text:
Minor Violation                                                              71111.21N.05
Minor Violation: During performance of Procedure FPSP-RO-10, “Fire Water Suppression
System Flow Test,” on May 08, 2023, per WO 52965257-01, unexpected results were
encountered during Section 5.4 and 5.5 for the inside loop path 2 and 3 when compared to
the previous 2017 flow performance test. Path 2 was the branch connection to the turbine
building fire hoses through valve MV-FP283 and MV-FP1162. Path 3 was the branch
connection to the transformer deluge through valves MV-FP282 and MV-FP117.

The flow tests for these two paths have only been performed twice since they were
added to the procedure in 2016. In the 2017 tests, the inside loop path 2 flow was
1099 gallon-per-minute (gpm) and the path 3 flow was 1135 gpm. In the 2023 tests,
the inside loop path 2 flow was 832 gpm and the path 3 flow was 774 gpm. CR PAL-01124
“FPSP-RO-10 Fire Suppression Water System Flow Test Degraded,” was initiated at that
time and noted there maybe flow restrictions in the fire system cross tie or associated piping.



The CR was closed to work request (WR) 01124 to inspect MV-FP283 internals to check
for obstruction.

During the inspectors’ review of Procedure FPSP-RO-10, the inspectors noticed that the
procedure did not include acceptance criteria for testing the fire water suppression flow for
these two paths.

The site noted that WO 00589203 for WR 01124 was required to be completed during the
fire protection system return-to-service plan or a justification would be needed.

Screening: The inspectors determined that the performance deficiency for failure to include
acceptance criteria in Procedure FPSP-RO-10 for testing inside loop paths 2 and 3 was minor
because the unacceptable results for paths 2 and 3 were recognized by the licensee and
documented in CR PAL-01124.

Enforcement: License Condition 2.C.(3) stated that Palisades Energy shall implement
and maintain in effect all previsions of the approved fire protection program. Procedure
FPSP-RO-10 was the implementing procedure for testing the fire water suppression system
flow.

Contrary to the above, Procedure FPSP-RO-10 failed to include the acceptance criteria
for the inside loop paths 2 and 3. The licensee documented this issue in CR 25015259
“FPSP-RO-10 did not include Acceptance Criteria for Flow Test.”

This failure to comply with the above requirements constitutes a minor violation that is
not subject to enforcement action in accordance with the NRC’s Enforcement Policy.

title: Minor Violation · 71111.21N.05
text:
Minor Violation                                                                  71111.21N.05

Minor Violation: The inspectors requested the previous work orders documentation of the
two diesel driven fire water pump (P-9B and P-41,) engine (K-5 and K-10) inspection, and
preventive maintenance which was completed during the shutdown period. The site failed
to locate three work orders in records including WO 00584081-01 for Pump P-9B, 2023
WO 50083624-01 for P-41, and 2025 WO 52990823-01 for P-41. Upon further searching,
two of the three missing WOs were located outside of the document control and records
management process. The 2023 WO 50083624-01 for P-41/K-10 engine inspection was not
located by the exit for this inspection.

Screening: The inspectors determined that the performance deficiency was minor since the
most recent completed work order in 2025 for P-41/K-10 was available and provided
assurance that the engine was successfully inspected.

Enforcement: License Condition 2.C.(3) stated Palisades Energy shall implement and
maintain in effect all provisions of the approved fire protection program. Site Procedure
FPIP-4, “Fire Protection Systems and Fire Protection Equipment,” Section 20.2 was the
implementing procedure of the approved fire protection program and required records to
be filed in accordance with the document control and records management process.

Procedure DSP-RM-001, “Document Control and Records Management Process,”
which required official records to be transmitted within 30 days after record completion.

Contrary to the above requirements, the licensee failed to maintain the official records for
WO 50083624-01 for P-41/K-10 fire engine inspection. The licensee entered this issue into
their corrective action program and initiated CR 25015056 “Failure to meet Procedure
DSP-RM-001 Requirement for Transmitting Official Records.”

This failure to comply with DSP-RM-001 constitutes a minor violation that is not subject
to enforcement action in accordance with the NRC’s Enforcement Policy.

title: Minor Violation · 71111.21N.05
text:
Minor Violation                                                                 71111.21N.05
Minor Violation: During a walkdown of the Auxiliary Feedwater Pump P-8D enclosure, the
inspectors questioned the presence of combustibles in the 5-foot perimeter. Combustibles
included a temporary metal office with windows within 3 feet of the east side of the P-8D
enclosure/trailer and additional combustibles laying on the ground.

Attachment 1 of Procedure ENG-329, “Control of Combustibles,” identified Fire Area 59,
the auxiliary feedwater Pump P-8D enclosure/trailer, as Level 1 combustible area including
a 5-foot perimeter surrounding this fire area. Compensatory measures were required for any
transient combustibles in the area.

Screening: The inspectors determined that the failure to maintain Level 1 combustible
controls for P-8D was a minor performance deficiency since pump P-8D was not required to
be functional for the current plant shutdown conditions.

Enforcement: License Condition 2.C.(3) stated Palisades Energy shall implement and
maintain in effect all provisions of the approved fire protection program. Site Procedure
ENG-329, “Control of Combustibles,” Revision 2 was the implementing procedure of the
approved fire protection program. Attachment 1 of ENG-329 identified Fire Area 59,
Pump P-8D as a Level 1 combustible area including a 5-foot perimeter surrounding this
fire area.

Contrary to this requirement, as of December 9, 2025, transient combustibles were found
within 3 feet of P-8D trailer, and no compensatory measures were established.

In response to the inspectors’ concern, the site-initiated CR 25015052 “Combustible Materials
were Found Contrary to ENG-329.” The site removed the combustible materials and planned
to remove the office building prior to declaring the P-8D system functional.





This failure to comply with ENG-329 constitutes a minor violation that is not subject to
enforcement action in accordance with the NRC’s Enforcement Policy.

title: Minor Violation · 71111.21N.05
text:
Minor Violation                                                                   71111.21N.05
 Minor Violation: Palisades had the option of hydrostatically pressure testing fire hoses
 every three years or replacing them with new fire hoses every five years. Work Order
 (WO) 53007241-01 was initiated to replace all fire hoses prior to the site entering technical
 specifications on August 26, 2025. Due to site procurement delays, all fire hoses were not
 replaced or hydrostatically pressure tested as required with some fire hoses last replaced
 in 2018.

  Prior to this inspection, condition report (CR) 25014235, “Fire Hose Replacement or
  Hydrostatic Test not Complete,” was initiated on November 11, 2025. This CR identified
  scheduling conflicts prevented hydrostatic pressure testing of fire hoses which were not
  replaced. At this time, the site failed to establish compensatory actions for the affected fire
  hoses as required per Procedure FPIP-4, “Fire Protection Systems and Fire Protection
  Equipment,” Revision 45.

  The inspectors questioned the number and installed location of the expired fire hoses.
  In response to the inspectors’ question, the site identified 30 fire hoses which failed to be
  tested or replaced at the required frequency including some located inside the power block.





Screening: The inspectors determined that the performance deficiency for the failure to test or
replace fire hoses at the required frequency was a minor since the fire brigade were trained to
bring a high-rise fire hose when responding to fire events. The installed expired fire hoses
would still perform their function at some capacity, and due to the current defueled state of
the plant there was no potential release from the core in event of fire.

Enforcement: License Condition 2.C.(3) stated that Palisades Energy shall implement and
maintain in effect all provisions of the approved fire protection program. Site Procedure
FPIP-4, “Fire Protection Systems and Fire Protection Equipment,” Revision 45 was the
implementing procedure of the approved fire protection program which required licensee to
establish compensatory actions for the affected fire hoses.

As a result of this inspection, all power block fire hoses were replaced upon discovery and
compensatory measure, including fire tours, in accordance with FPIP-4 were established
for the remaining fire hose locations. CR 25015303 “Fire Hose to be Hydrostatic Tested
or Replaced,” was initiated on December 17, 2025, documenting this issue.

This failure to comply with requirement of FPIP-4 and establish compensatory actions
constitutes a minor violation that is not subject to enforcement action in accordance with
the NRC’s Enforcement Policy.

title: Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation · 71124.08
text:
Licensee-Identified Non-Cited Violation                                           71124.08
This violation of very low safety significance was identified by the licensee and has been
entered into the licensee corrective action program and is being treated as a non-cited
violation, consistent with Section 2.3.2 of the Enforcement Policy.
Violation: Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part 71.5 requires, in part,
that each licensee who transports licensed material outside the site of usage comply with the
applicable requirements of the Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations in 49 CFR
Parts 171 through 180. 49 CFR 173.441 requires, in part, that exclusive use shipment
radiation levels not exceed 10 mrem/h at any point two meters from the outer lateral surfaces
of the vehicle (excluding the top and underside of the vehicle). Contrary to the above,
on September 23, 2025, the licensee failed to comply with the applicable requirements of the
DOT regulations in 49 CFR Parts 171 through 180 as required by 10 CFR 71.5. Specifically,
the licensee failed to comply with 49 CFR 173.441 when the licensee transported radioactive
waste off-site via exclusive use with dose rates of up to 16.2 mrem/hr at two meters from the
lateral surfaces (sides) of the vehicle.

Significance/Severity: Green. The performance deficiency was assessed using Inspection
Manual Chapter (IMC) 0609, Appendix D as a finding in transportation or Part 61. An external
radiation limit was exceeded in a location accessible by the public. However, the IMC allows
for other considerations to be taken into account when determining if an issue reaches the
White threshold. In this instance, the shipment was an exclusive use shipment and surveys
conducted upon return of the transport vehicle that were conducted with a survey instrument
that averages dose rates over a larger cross-sectional area indicated maximum dose rates of
10 mrem/hr at two meters from the lateral surfaces of the vehicle. With these considerations
taken into account, this issue was determined to be of very low safety significance (Green).

Corrective Action References: AR 25012715
